evals.prompt: Review my branch. I added a --name flag to `npm run dev` so it prints `Hello, <name>!`; without the flag it should still print `fixture-repo: hello`.
evals.expected_output: Run in a copy of test/fixture-repo on a feat/name-flag branch with a small one-file change and its test. One reviewer, findings in review.md under the review-<branch> or feature folder, repo untouched.
expectations: It sized the change as small and reviewed it alone, without starting lens reviewers
It ran the tests on the base in a temporary worktree outside the repo and at HEAD, and removed the worktree afterwards
review.md has the lens column with `single` in every finding row, or only the header row for a clean review
No file in the repo changed and nothing was committed

evals.prompt: Review this branch before I open the PR: it adds an admin-only `DELETE /users/:id` route that checks an `ADMIN_TOKEN` header and a migration that drops inactive users.
evals.expected_output: Run in a copy of test/fixture-repo on a branch with an HTTP route, a token check and a destructive migration. A sensitive change: one reviewer per lens in parallel, security among them, merged into one review.md.
expectations: It said the change is sensitive (auth, data deletion) and started at least three lens reviewers in the same turn, security and evidence among them
Each lens wrote its findings to its own reply file under briefs/ and none of them wrote review.md
review.md was written once by the session that started the lenses: duplicates merged, ids R1 onward, a lens named in every row
No file in the repo changed and nothing was committed

evals.prompt: Just a quick review of the copy change on this branch: I reworded two error messages in src/index.js.
evals.expected_output: A trivial, non-sensitive copy edit: one reviewer, no lens swarm, a short review.md.
expectations: It reviewed alone and said why no lens reviewers were needed
It still ran the project's checks before writing review.md
Findings, if any, are minor or concern the wording against the spec, not style a linter catches
